messages:
nora: Quick follow-up from today's quota smoothing sync. I'm proposing a preemptive-eviction layer to protect tail latencies and fairness when tenants spike. Short thread with tradeoffs + sketch.

diego: tl;dr? what's preemptive-eviction exactly?

nora: Idea: when global load trends indicate a tenant will breach its fair share, admission can instantly apply a lightweight preemptive-eviction marker to some in-flight low-priority requests from that tenant (soft revoke) to free capacity before hard denials cascade.

sasha: sounds risky UX-wise. users might see partially completed responses. How do we ensure idempotency and clear traceability?

nora: eviction only targets stateless idempotent calls (embeddings, low-priority batch jobs) initially. Each request gets a short-lived admission token. Preemptive-eviction sends a revoke event referencing request_id and a reason_code. Sidecars must handle revoke by attempting graceful cancel + credit restoration.

diego: tradeoffs: pro = avoids global thrash and keeps p95/p99 sane; con = complexity in bookkeeping and potential increased user-visible errors.

sasha: can we make it conservative: only evict if predicted wait > X ms and tenant exceeded a sustained delta above fair share? Also require confidence score from anomaly detector > 0.9.

ben: implementable sketch: 1) admission consults local fairness window and smoothing predictor; 2) if forecast breach and request is evictable, mark request with evictable=true and optimistic admit; 3) if global reconciler confirms overdraw, publish revoke for a subset ranked by low-priority and age.

nora: API hint for revokes: POST /v1/evict with body {request_id, tenant, reason_code, confidence}. Response 200 means sidecar acknowledged. Keep reason_code small set: [BUDGET_PREEMPT, HOTSPOT_REBALANCE, FRAUD_CONFIRM].

diego: telemetry: track evictable_admits, evictions_sent, evictions_acked, revoked_retries, post-eviction latency delta, and false-eviction complaints. Alert if false-evictions > 0.2%.

sasha: rollout: lab sim -> canary 1% focusing on embeddings -> expose header X-Evicted: yes/no so clients can surface helpful UX. Also docs for partners.

ben: safety net: if sidecar doesn't ack eviction, admission will fallback to marking tenant as soft-throttled and rely on quota-shard to enforce. No silent silent failures.

nora: ergonomics: tenants should be able to opt out of preemptive-eviction and opt into stricter hard-deny SLAs for enterprise. Default: opt-in for low-priority workloads.

diego: one more: fairness scheduler should incorporate a smoothing window (exponential decay) so short bursts don't immediately trigger evictions. Suggest window=15s and decay factor 0.6 as starting point.

sasha: +1. Also include reason_code in user-facing support logs for appeal.

ops-bot: scheduled: canary pipeline queued for branch quota-smoothing/preemptive-evict in 8m. :hourglass:

nora: assigning: diego -> predictor tuning + telemetry, sasha -> sidecar revoke handler + UX header, ben -> reconciler + reason_code enum and proto. I'll draft the RFC addendum and proto later today. If no objections by EOD we'll start the canary.

ben: +1.

nora: thanks all, short RFC addendum incoming.
